symptoms.title: Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”
steps: This is the SmartScreen warning: it appears for any executable that is not signed yet or not yet known to Microsoft.
First check the file is genuine (see “Check the file is genuine”).
Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

symptoms.title: My antivirus blocks or deletes Dynamics.exe
steps: Executables built with PyInstaller are often flagged by mistake: this is a common false positive.
Check the file is genuine: same SHA-256 checksum as on the Install page, and a valid GitHub attestation.
If both checks pass, restore the file from quarantine and add an exclusion.
Report the false positive to your antivirus vendor: it helps every other user.

symptoms.title: Check the file is genuine
steps: In PowerShell, in the download folder: `Get-FileHash .\Dynamics.exe -Algorithm SHA256`.
Compare the result with the SHA-256 shown on the Install page: they must be identical.
With the GitHub CLI, `gh attestation verify .\Dynamics.exe --repo Blackoune/OBS-Dynamics` confirms the file was built by GitHub from the public code.
If a check fails, delete the file and download it only from the Install page.

symptoms.title: I use a Mac
steps: OBS Dynamics only runs on Windows 10 and 11 for now: it relies on Windows-only features.
There is no Mac version and no Mac file. Be wary of any file claiming to be one.

symptoms.title: The status shows “Monitoring active (OBS: …)” or the app never connects
steps: Check that OBS Studio is running.
In OBS: **Tools → WebSocket Server Settings**, the server must be enabled.
Compare the port with the one in the **Settings** tab (4455 by default).
Copy the password again from **Show Connect Info** and save it again in **Settings**.
A third-party firewall may block `localhost:4455`: allow OBS.

symptoms.title: The password seems lost after copying .env from another PC
steps: This is expected: the encryption is tied to the original Windows account.
Enter the password again in **Settings**.

symptoms.title: Scene menus show “(not connected to OBS)”
steps: Start monitoring.
Wait for the “OBS connected” status.
Reopen the game’s settings.

symptoms.title: A Steam game is not found by the scan
steps: Check that it is actually installed, not just in your Steam library.
Otherwise, add it as **Manual (exe)**.

symptoms.title: The game is running but its card stays “Idle”
steps: For a manual game, the executable name must exactly match the one in **Task Manager → Details**, extension included.
Some games start through a launcher: enter the game’s own executable, not the launcher’s.

symptoms.title: The scene does not switch between menu and gameplay
steps: Monitoring must be started and OBS connected.
The game must have a scene for each state.
Open **Check framing** then **Test on current screen** with the game displayed. A score below the threshold (0.8 by default) explains the issue.
If the lead is reported as too small, take more distinct screenshots: a full-screen menu versus an in-game HUD, for example.

symptoms.title: The scene switches at the wrong time
steps: Some fragments probably land on the background.
In **Check framing**, tick the badly placed frames then **Recompute without ticked**, or place manual zones on the interface.
As a last resort, raise the threshold slightly in **Settings**.

symptoms.title: I have several screens and nothing is detected
steps: Capture uses Windows’ **main display**.
Show the game on that display.

symptoms.title: No cover art for a non-Steam game
steps: Add a free `RAWG_API_KEY` to the `.env` file.

symptoms.title: The key combination does nothing
steps: The browser source must be open in OBS: without it, the log says “no browser source open”.
Another program may capture the same combination: pick a different one.
If the combination field shows “pynput missing”, reinstall the dependencies: `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

symptoms.title: The browser source stays empty or shows an error
steps: The app must be running: it serves the page.
Check that the pasted URL is exactly the one shown, with `127.0.0.1` and the right port.
A yellow banner in the tab means the port changed: copy the URLs again.
A source opened before the app started shows an error until it is refreshed. Tick **Refresh browser when scene becomes active** in the source properties.

symptoms.title: A shortcut’s sound cannot be heard
steps: In the browser source properties, tick **Control audio via OBS**.
Check the source level in the OBS audio mixer.

symptoms.title: Drag and drop does not work
steps: It needs the `tkinterdnd2` package, included in the executable.
Without it, the drop zone stays clickable and opens the file picker.

symptoms.title: The status stays “Error — reconnecting…”
steps: Check the channel spelling: the name only, not the URL.
Check your internet connection. The app reconnects on its own, waiting a little longer each time.

symptoms.title: The chat link no longer works
steps: It was probably regenerated.
Copy the link shown in the app and paste it into OBS again.

symptoms.title: “Windows media interface unavailable”
steps: The `winrt-*` packages are missing (install from source): `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

symptoms.title: “Windows is not answering”
steps: Windows’ media session service is stuck.
Close and reopen the app. If the problem persists, restart Windows.

symptoms.title: No session detected while music is playing
steps: Pause then resume playback.
Click **Refresh**.

symptoms.title: The waveform stays flat
steps: The player must output sound: volume not muted in the Windows mixer.
In a browser, the waveform follows all of the browser’s sound.

symptoms.title: The card is cropped in OBS
steps: Enlarge the browser source to the size shown by the app.
Or use 1132 × 383, which covers every case.
